## Entry detail (7a)

The one screen where looking at the food is the point, so the photo gets 300px and a top-to-bottom scrim carrying the date and title over it. `‹ TODAY` returns to the day you came from; `EDIT` top-right.

Below, in order: three macro tiles → what you typed → **estimate vs saved** → metadata → actions.

### Estimate vs saved — the important block

| Row | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `MODEL SAID` | `620 · 34P · 6F` |
| `YOU SAVED` | `540 · 41P · 6F` |

Tagged `YOU EDITED THIS` in over-target orange, with: *The original response is kept for every entry. It is the only honest way to measure whether the estimates are any good.*

This surfaces `ai_raw_response` to the user rather than keeping it purely as a backend column. Two reasons: it makes the app's honesty legible, and it is the only screen where you can eyeball whether the model is systematically over- or under-estimating. Hide it and nobody ever looks.

Metadata rows: `SOURCE` (camera / library) · `CONFIDENCE` (medium — portion) · `DAY` with `MOVE TO ANOTHER DAY ›`, which repoints the entry at a different `DailyLog`.

Actions: `RE-ANALYZE THIS PHOTO` (secondary) and `DELETE ENTRY` (orange hairline outline, never a filled red button).

## Delete entry (7b)

**Names consequences instead of asking "are you sure".**

> Delete this entry?
> The photo comes out of storage too, and today's totals drop by 540 kcal. It was not the day's only entry, so your streak is unaffected.

Then, in a nested panel: *If it had been the last entry of the day, the day would leave your streak — worth saying out loud rather than letting the number quietly change.*

That second sentence exists because of a real edge case in doc 07: deleting a day's last entry changes the streak. Silently altering a number the user cares about is the worst version of that; the copy must be conditional on whether this is the last entry.

Buttons: `DELETE IT` (orange fill) / `KEEP IT`. The destructive action is not the visually dominant one.

Implementation: deletion must also remove the R2 object. Orphaned images are a slow storage leak and a privacy problem.

## Settings (7c)

Six groups, in this order:

**Account** — email with a `VERIFIED` badge, Apple ID `LINKED`, change password.

**Targets** — current three numbers inline, then `ADJUST` and `HISTORY`. Adjust reuses the onboarding adjust screen from doc 15; same component, different entry point.

**Apple Health** — a real toggle for write-only sync, subtitled *Write only. Nothing is read back.* Plus `Sync past entries · 142 ENTRIES` for the backfill from doc 10. Ship this section disabled until E10.

**AI usage** — `48 / 300` with a progress bar and: *Photo estimates and advice requests both count. Resets on the 1st. The ceiling exists to stop abuse, not to ration normal use.* Showing the quota before it is hit is what makes the limit feel like a policy rather than a bug.

**Privacy** — privacy policy link, a plain-language *Where your photos go* block (stored privately in R2, sent to an AI provider for estimation, never used for advertising), and the stored time zone.

**Danger** — `Delete my account` in orange.

Footer: version and build, `SIGN OUT`.

## Target history (7d)

One card per `TargetVersion`, newest first: date range, a `MANUAL` / `ONBOARDING AI` badge, the three numbers in their macro colours, and a line on why it changed.

Header copy carries the model: *Every change writes a version. Days already logged keep the version that was live at the time, so nothing behind you gets rewritten.*

Small feature, disproportionate value — it makes the slowly-changing-dimension pattern tangible, and on a long cut it is genuinely interesting to look at.

## Delete account (7e)

Required in-app by both stores. Presented as a timeline rather than a warning:

| When | What |
| -- | -- |
| `NOW` | Signed out everywhere, can no longer log in |
| `30d` | Entries and photos held, recoverable by email. Nothing visible to you |
| `THEN` | Purged for good — database rows and every photo in storage |

Then the reasoning, stated for the record: *The grace period is deliberate. Destroying a year of logging on one tap is a bad experience and a worse support conversation.*

A typed `DELETE` confirmation gates the primary button, which stays visually inert (muted fill, muted text) until the field matches. `KEEP MY ACCOUNT` is the outlined escape.

## Decision recorded: no separate first-run screen

A dedicated "nothing logged ever" screen was designed and then **cut**. The home screen already teaches the loop — one big number, one button labelled Log food — and a separate screen means a different mental model on day one plus a second layout to maintain, for something each user sees once.

The real problem it was solving is narrower: on day one the ring reads `2150 KCAL LEFT` at 100%, which is visually identical to a perfect day, and zeroed tiles read as broken rather than empty. Fix as a **variant of the home screen**, not a screen:

* Ring centre reads `NOTHING LOGGED YET`, track only, no fill
* Tiles show `—`, not `0`
* Where the entry list would be: one line — *Photograph what you're about to eat and the numbers get filled in.*
* Log food button unchanged, same position

**Not yet built.** This is the one outstanding item in the home screen design.
